title: Farukhsiyar’s Dragged Death and the Opening of the Khalsa Aftermath

blocks.text: The page fulfills Banda Singh's prophetic warning by narrating how the emperor was dragged after falling with his foot remained in the stirrup. Farukhsiyar's humiliation and death are presented as the reversal of the vengeance he had earlier displayed against the Sikhs.

The text then closes the episode with calendrical detail and the sense that Banda Singh's words came true in history rather than only in legend. The emperor who ordered public degradation is himself reduced to a public example of overturned fortune.

From there the book opens a new question: Where did the Khalsa stay after getting Banda Singh executed? That turn shifts the focus away from the fallen emperor and toward the survival of the Panth after the destruction of its most famous commander.
